action_criteria.expected_evidence: Right frontal 5.2 cm mass centered in the precentral and middle frontal gyri with thick irregular ring and nodular enhancement, central necrosis, restricted diffusion in the enhancing rim, vasogenic edema across the genu of the corpus callosum and 8 mm leftward midline shift
action_criteria.label: Order MRI brain with and without gadolinium contrast (tumor protocol with DWI, FLAIR, post-contrast T1) to characterize the right frontal lesion, define mass effect, and plan surgery
action_criteria.rationale: Contrast MRI with diffusion and FLAIR characterizes the lesion and its mass effect, identifies the enhancing target and plans the surgical approach (EANO 2021).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: rCBV ratio 3.8 in the enhancing rim with a low-perfusion necrotic core, supporting a high-grade neoplasm and targeting tissue sampling
action_criteria.label: Order MR perfusion imaging (DSC perfusion) to assess tumor vascularity and target highest-grade region for biopsy
action_criteria.rationale: Perfusion supports a high-grade neoplasm and identifies the most vascular region to sample; tissue decides the diagnosis.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Cho/NAA 9.0 with lipid-lactate in the enhancing component and raised choline in the perilesional FLAIR region
action_criteria.label: Order MR spectroscopy (1H-MRS) to characterize tumor metabolic profile
action_criteria.rationale: Spectroscopy supports a high-grade neoplasm and shows infiltration beyond the enhancing margin; tissue decides the diagnosis.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No extracranial primary malignancy identified, supporting primary brain tumor as the working diagnosis
action_criteria.label: Order CT chest/abdomen/pelvis as staging to exclude an extracranial primary if a solitary metastasis is on the differential
action_criteria.rationale: A former smoker with a family history of lung cancer: staging CT excludes an extracranial primary if a solitary metastasis is considered.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Glucose 129 mg/dL and HbA1c 7.2% in known type 2 diabetes, relevant to dexamethasone; sodium, platelets and coagulation normal (INR 1.0): no laboratory contraindication to surgery
action_criteria.label: Order pre-operative laboratory workup: CBC, comprehensive metabolic panel, coagulation studies (PT/INR, aPTT), and type & screen in anticipation of surgical biopsy/resection
action_criteria.rationale: Surgery and corticosteroids are planned; coagulation, platelets, electrolytes, glucose and a group and screen are needed first.

action_criteria.label: Score performance status (Karnofsky and ECOG) at this visit
action_criteria.rationale: The choice between standard and hypofractionated chemoradiotherapy depends on age and Karnofsky performance status (EANO 2021).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Left-hand motor activation displaced posteromedially about 8 mm from the enhancing margin; left-hemisphere language dominance (laterality index 0.85)
action_criteria.label: Order functional MRI (motor and language mapping) before resection of the right precentral tumor
action_criteria.rationale: The tumor involves the right precentral gyrus; motor and language mapping defines the resection margin (EANO 2021).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Right corticospinal tract displaced but continuous, about 5 mm from the enhancing margin in the corona radiata
action_criteria.label: Order DTI tractography of the right corticospinal tract before resection
action_criteria.rationale: The tumor and its edema extend into the right corona radiata; tractography locates the corticospinal tract (EANO 2021).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Integrated diagnosis Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, CNS WHO grade 4 with IDH1 R132H negative, ATRX retained, MGMT promoter unmethylated
action_criteria.label: Obtain tissue by maximal safe resection of the right frontal lesion, or stereotactic biopsy if resection is not safely feasible, for an integrated histomolecular diagnosis with IDH1 R132H immunohistochemistry, ATRX immunohistochemistry and MGMT promoter methylation
action_criteria.rationale: Surgery is the first option for a resectable glioma and should be as extensive as safely possible (AIOM; EANO 2021). Only tissue establishes the integrated diagnosis and the molecular results that select treatment.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Steroid hyperglycemia on metformin and NSAID plus steroid GI risk identified; levetiracetam free of relevant interactions
action_criteria.label: Check interactions of dexamethasone and levetiracetam with the current medicines (metformin, ibuprofen, amlodipine, lisinopril, atorvastatin)
action_criteria.rationale: Dexamethasone worsens glycemic control and adds GI bleeding risk with NSAIDs; enzyme-inducing antiseizure drugs are avoided.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not perform lumbar puncture: the 8 mm midline shift creates a risk of herniation.
Do not initiate definitive tumor-directed therapy (radiation, temozolomide, alkylating chemotherapy) before tissue diagnosis is established
Do not start therapeutic anticoagulation without a clear thromboembolic indication, given upcoming neurosurgical intervention and bleeding risk
required_recommendations: Refer urgently to neurosurgery for maximal safe resection of the right frontal lesion, with preoperative functional MRI and DTI tractography and intraoperative mapping, with stereotactic biopsy if resection is not safely feasible; send the specimen for an integrated histomolecular diagnosis (WHO CNS5).

Start dexamethasone for symptomatic vasogenic edema (for example 4 mg every 6 to 8 hours after a loading dose when mass effect is marked) at the lowest effective dose, with glucose monitoring and gastric protection, and taper after surgery.

Start antiseizure treatment with levetiracetam for the documented focal seizure with left arm onset and bilateral tonic-clonic spread; this is treatment of tumor-related epilepsy, not prophylaxis. Avoid enzyme-inducing antiseizure drugs (phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital), which lower dexamethasone and chemotherapy exposure.
Monitor capillary glucose at least every 6 hours on dexamethasone and adjust the antihyperglycemic regimen (metformin, adding insulin if needed), given type 2 diabetes with HbA1c 7.2%.
Stop as-needed ibuprofen while on dexamethasone and before surgery (GI bleeding and platelet effect).

After the integrated diagnosis, refer to the neuro-oncology multidisciplinary team; for glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype at age 70 or under with KPS 70 or more, radiotherapy 60 Gy in 30 fractions with concomitant and adjuvant temozolomide (Stupp 2005; EANO 2021).

differential.key_features: Former smoker with a family history of lung cancer, but no known primary; staging CT chest, abdomen and pelvis negative; infiltrative margins with spread across the genu of the corpus callosum favor a primary glioma; tissue shows a GFAP-positive glial neoplasm
Necrosis and microvascular proliferation occur in both; IDH1 R132H negative with no IDH1/IDH2 mutation on sequencing and ATRX retained exclude it
Immunocompetent; thick irregular ring enhancement with central necrosis, rather than homogeneous enhancement with diffuse restriction; tissue shows a glial neoplasm
Afebrile, WBC 7.5, CRP 4.2; restricted diffusion in the enhancing rim rather than the core and rCBV 3.8 in the rim argue against pus
Closed thick ring with nodular enhancement, central necrosis and marked mass effect at 58 are atypical; demyelination usually shows an open ring and low rCBV

key_clinical_evidence: Progressive morning headache, new left arm weakness and a first focal seizure with bilateral spread in an adult call for urgent contrast-enhanced brain MRI

The MRI shows a right frontal mass in the precentral and middle frontal gyri with thick irregular ring enhancement, central necrosis, rim restricted diffusion, edema across the genu and 8 mm midline shift: a high-grade neoplasm on imaging
Perfusion (rCBV 3.8) and spectroscopy (Cho/NAA 9.0, lipid-lactate) support a high-grade neoplasm and target sampling; they do not grade the tumor
Symptomatic edema with 8 mm midline shift: dexamethasone, and lumbar puncture is contraindicated

Only tissue gives the integrated diagnosis: IDH1 R132H negative at age 58, ATRX retained, with microvascular proliferation and necrosis, is glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, CNS WHO grade 4; MGMT is unmethylated
The tumor involves the precentral gyrus and abuts the corticospinal tract, so functional MRI and DTI plan a maximal safe resection; at 58 with KPS 70 the standard after surgery is the Stupp regimen
Off-pathway advanced imaging (DaTscan, amyloid PET, FDG-PET, carotid duplex, transcranial Doppler) addresses other questions and adds cost without informing glioma management
A focal seizure with bilateral spread is tumor-related epilepsy: levetiracetam is treatment, not prophylaxis, and enzyme-inducing drugs are avoided because of dexamethasone and temozolomide

patient.history_present_illness: Mr. Robert Dalton is a 58-year-old right-handed man with a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and hyperlipidemia who presents to the emergency department after a witnessed generalized tonic-clonic seizure at home. His wife reports that over the past three weeks, he has been complaining of progressively worsening headaches, predominantly on the right side, which are worst in the early morning and occasionally wake him from sleep. He has been using over-the-counter ibuprofen with only marginal relief. She also noticed that about two weeks ago, he began having difficulty using his left hand at work, dropping objects and struggling with fine motor tasks such as buttoning his shirt. She describes him as being somewhat more forgetful and 'not himself' over the past ten days, occasionally repeating questions and seeming confused about appointments. This morning at approximately 07:15, while eating breakfast, his wife observed his left arm begin to shake rhythmically, followed within thirty seconds by his eyes rolling back and a generalized convulsion lasting approximately ninety seconds. He was postictal and confused for about fifteen minutes afterward. EMS was called and he was transported to the emergency department. On arrival, he was alert and conversant but had a persistent mild headache. He denies any prior seizure history, recent head trauma, febrile illness, vision changes, nausea, or vomiting. He has not had any recent weight loss or night sweats. His wife reports no recent travel or sick contacts. A non-contrast CT scan obtained in the emergency department revealed a large right frontal mass with partly hyperdense components and surrounding hypodensity consistent with edema, and approximately 8 mm of midline shift to the left. He was admitted to the neurology service for further workup.
